items.action: Build after upgrading, and rename or mark `override` every member of yours the compiler reports as colliding.
items.appliesWhen: Only a class of yours that extends one of the listed components. Template users of those components need nothing; subclassing a DS component is unsupported.
items.pitfall: `protected` and `private` are no protection: a redeclared member collides exactly as a public one does.
items.verify: The app builds with no TS4114 or TS2416 against a DS base class.
items.note: DrawerComponent and BottomSheetComponent gained preview; TooltipDirective gained dsTooltipTextElement and textElement. The compiler names every collision.

informational.text: A dsTooltipWhenClipped host that cannot take focus opens on Tab only when its nearest focusable ancestor is a control: a native a[href], button, input, select, textarea or summary, a table row, or an element with the role button, link, tab, option, menuitem, menuitemcheckbox, menuitemradio, row, gridcell, combobox, checkbox, radio, switch or treeitem. A focusable container such as a ds-tabs panel, a scroll region or a role-less div with tabindex="0" opens nothing. A role-less focusable element that acts as a control discloses again once it carries its role.
informational.verify: Tab onto a ds-tabs panel holding a clipped dsTooltipWhenClipped label and confirm no tooltip opens; Tab onto a ds-button or ds-select trigger holding a clipped label and confirm its tooltip opens, and that a mouse click on it opens none.

informational.text: The ds-table scroll box is position: relative, so the hidden header label of a column with screenReaderLabel and no label is clipped with the rows and no longer widens the page when the table overflows its container. An element positioned absolutely inside a cell template with no positioned ancestor of its own resolves against that scroll box.
informational.verify: At a viewport narrower than the table, put a column with screenReaderLabel and no label past the container's edge and confirm document.documentElement.scrollWidth equals clientWidth while the table still scrolls horizontally inside its box.
